title: Traffic slab orchestration and psychology notes
content:
Purpose:
This note collects informal lab observations, coordination rituals, and psych-safety cues for running traffic-slab based canaries and A/B experiments across Console, Dedicated, and Private customers. Goal is to give PMs, Eng, SRE, and CS a compact operational playbook that emphasizes human handoffs and metric-led rollback decisions rather than a fully prescriptive flow.

Key concept: traffic slab = an orthogonal partition of traffic by a deterministic selector (header, cookie cohort, geo slice, product route) that receives a contiguous fraction of requests for a limited duration window. Slabs let us test variants in surface area smaller than classical cohort sampling and enable fast sequential exposure across slabs.

Why slabs and rituals?
- Slabs reduce noisiness from user churn and preserve temporal locality for model cache effects.
- Rituals (check-in, greenlight, escalation) reduce cognitive overhead when many teams observe the same experiment.
- Psychological framing matters: operators must experience low friction to revert and high confidence to progress.

High-level slab protocol (short):
1) Preflight (T-72 to T-4 hours):
   - Define slab selector: header X-Exp-Group, route path, or cookie cohort. Write a one-line selector and register in experiment metadata.
   - Identify owners: product lead, runtime owner, SRE oncall, CS lead. Capture contact + pager.
   - Acceptance metrics (primary + guardrails) declared in plain English and numeric thresholds. Example: non-inferiority on median p95 latency (+15% allowed), top-line acceptance on conversion delta > +1.5% (A/B), safety guardrail: API error rate <= baseline + 0.1pp.
   - Traffic schedule: slabs = [0.5%, 2%, 8%, 30%] with 30–90m dwell per slab. Document exact dwell.
   - Synthetic traffic harness prepared if integration touches edge caches.

2) Launch (T=0):
   - Create rollout job in Console with slab config and quick revert button visible to owners.
   - Start slab-0.5%: observe 15–30 minutes of live metrics and full tracing span capture. If no red flags, ceremony call (5m) to progress.

3) Progression heuristic (qualitative):
   - Fast check: UI cost and latency graphs within expected band, no spike in 5xx or model-level hallucination reports.
   - Quant gating: primary metric delta CI excludes harmful direction or stays within pre-declared tolerance. Use conservative Bayesian posterior if low sample.
   - Soft signoff: product + SRE. If disagreement, hold and run targeted diagnostics.

4) Rollback triggers (examples):
   - Absolute threshold breach (example: error rate > baseline + 0.5pp sustained 5m).
   - Latency p95 > baseline * 1.25 and correlated with token-per-request growth in traces.
   - User-facing regression flagged by CS with >5 escalations in 10 minutes.
   - Model quality drift on eval checksets beyond alert window.

Operational notes and psychology tips:
- Keep the revert path trivial: Console must show a single-click revert to previous model/route. People tolerate risk when the escape hatch is obvious.
- Do a short pre-launch dry-voice call (5m) where each owner states their single watch signal. This reduces diffusion of responsibility.
- Publicly declare a minimal observation window per slab (e.g., 30m) so progress cadence is predictable.
- Use explicit channel naming (e.g., #rollout-<slug>-live) and pin the primary metric charts + links at top of the channel.

Metrics to surface (dashboard staples):
- Primary: conversion / objective metric (A/B) or median scoring match rate (canary).
- Performance: p50/p95 latency, CPU/GPU slot wait, token throughput, median tokens-per-request.
- Reliability: 5xx count, dropped-connection rate, grpc timeout counts, queue length.
- Safety/Quality: safety filter hit-rate, hallucination flags (auto-eval), semantic-similarity regression count on golden prompts.
- Cost: incremental tokens and compute minutes for slab window.

Sampling & statistical notes:
- For very low baseline signal, prefer longer dwell vs larger slab width. Larger slab can amplify correlated cache effects and hide regressions that only appear at scale.
- When comparing A/B variants, pre-register the metric, analysis method, and whether sequential peeking is allowed. If sequential checks likely, use alpha spending corrections or Bayesian stopping rules.

Failure modes observed in experiments (lab notes):
- Double caching: model variant caused cache key changes leading to misleading latency improvements; debug by synthetic cold-run.
- Surface-level non-determinism: telemetry was missing trace IDs from private deployments; ensure trace propagation early.
- Psychological: teams advanced to next slab too early because progress calls lacked explicit negative criteria. Fix: require both owners to say "proceed" not silence.

Checklist (pre-launch):
- [ ] Slab selector string in metadata + doc link
- [ ] Owners + oncall listed
- [ ] Dashboard created and pinned in channel
- [ ] Synthetic harness for edge cases ready
- [ ] Revert playbook drafted (who, how, notify)
- [ ] Compliance/privacy review (if cohorting by sensitive attribute)
- [ ] Budget approval for expected incremental cost

Comms templates (short):
- Progress update (posted after each slab): "Slab 2% complete. Primary metric delta: +0.2pp (CI: -0.1, +0.5). Latency p95 +5%. No errors. Recommend proceed -> @sre @pm."
- Rollback announcement: "Action: rollback variant X -> stable. Trigger: p95 latency breach and > 0.2pp increase in 5xx. Timeline: reverting now; estimated 6m until new routing propagated. Notifying CS and oncall."

Post-mortem and learning capture:
- Always capture slab-level artifacts: sample traces, saved golden prompt outputs, and a tiny synthetic replay of traffic that reproduced the issue.
- For A/B, publish a simple summary: sample size, point estimate, CI, incremental cost, and decision (ship/iterate/rollback).

Open questions and next experiments (todo):
- Can we automate slab progression using a conservative RL agent that enforces minimum dwell and requires human override? (RF-876)
- Test slab width shaping: does exponential increase (0.5->2->8->30) outperform linear for model cache warmups? (run small offline sim)
- Define a lightweight privacy-safe slab selector pattern for enterprises that disallows user-level cookies.

Appendix: quick runbook snippet for oncall
- If alerted: check model variant id, slab selector, recent deploy PRs, and token-per-request. If 5xx spike, flip routing to previous variant and notify the PM and CS.

End notes:
This doc is intentionally conversational. If we like this format, we should fold a distilled checklist into the Console rollout wizard. For now, use as a coordination cheat-sheet and paste into experiment channels when launching slabs.
